minor.issue: Returns a bare JSON array (145 items) instead of an object wrapper. Consistent with /api/fonts returning {fonts:[...]}? Inconsistent — currencies is a bare list, fonts is a wrapped object. Consider {currencies:[...]} for symmetry, or change /api/fonts to a bare list. Minor DX/consistency issue.

Storage is fetched from external Emergent Object Storage service on every request via _init_storage() → requests.post(...) synchronously (blocking event loop). Under load or if storage_key becomes stale, this will block. Consider using aiohttp/httpx.AsyncClient for storage calls and cache storage_key more aggressively or refresh on-demand only.

_ensure_stripe_catalog() runs stripe.Product.list().auto_paging_iter() on EVERY first checkout in the process. This iterates ALL products in the Stripe account (potentially thousands) and does a linear scan for metadata.emergent_product_id. Consider caching the resolved price IDs in-memory once per process, or persisting them in Mongo after first resolution.

No auth. Anyone who knows a session_id can query its status. Session IDs are ~30 char random strings so brute force is not feasible, but consider requiring auth + workspace ownership check for defense-in-depth.

PIL renders synchronously (blocking event loop). Acceptable for MVP but a batch of concurrent downloads will starve other requests. Consider running in a thread executor (loop.run_in_executor) for a real production load.

When STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty (current state), signature verification is bypassed and any JSON body is trusted (`event = json.loads(payload.decode())`). This is a critical vulnerability in production. STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET must be set before going live — otherwise anyone can POST arbitrary webhook events to activate paid subscriptions on any workspace_id they know.

The <select data-testid=brand-currency-select> and brand-font-select render each <option> with a <span data-ve-dynamic=true> injected by the dev overlay tooling — this is a dev-mode-only warning from the ve tooling wrapping array items and does not affect production. React Router warns 'No routes matched location /logout' — the frontend has no /logout route wired. Users have to clear localStorage manually or use the sidebar/header sign-out (if present). Consider adding a /logout route that clears the promoos_token and redirects to /login.

action_items: HIGH (before production only, not blocking for MVP): Set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in backend/.env and enable signature verification. With current empty secret, /api/stripe/webhook accepts any unsigned JSON and can be abused to fake subscription activation on arbitrary workspace_ids. Not exploitable in the sandbox environment but must be fixed before switching STRIPE_MODE from 'test' to 'live'.
OPTIONAL: Add auth (or at least workspace-membership check) to GET /api/billing/status/{session_id} for defense-in-depth.
OPTIONAL: Cache resolved Stripe price IDs in Mongo (or in-process) instead of re-scanning stripe.Product.list() on every first checkout of a process.
OPTIONAL: Make storage upload/download async (aiohttp/httpx.AsyncClient) and offload PIL rendering to a thread executor to avoid blocking the FastAPI event loop.
OPTIONAL: Normalize response shape: /api/currencies returns a bare array while /api/fonts returns {fonts:[...]}. Pick one convention.
OPTIONAL: Add a /logout route that clears promoos_token and redirects to /login (currently /logout emits a router warning).

OPTIONAL (dev): The 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>' hydration warning is emitted by dev tooling injecting <span data-ve-dynamic> into every dynamic <option>. Confirm this is stripped in production builds; if not, wrap in a way that skips injection for <option> children.

CARRY-OVER from iter-5/6/7: Split /app/backend/server.py into router modules — server.py + extras.py now total ~3200 LOC. Suggested modules: routers/{auth,coupons,pos,journeys,ai,analytics,exports,embed,customers,admin,library,billing,uploads}.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: 2777 lines (previous iter: 2744, +33). extras.py: 467 lines (new). Total handlers now spread across 2 files, but server.py's monolithic size continues to grow. Router split remains overdue.

extras.py verify webhook: `event = json.loads(payload.decode())` when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty is a silent fallback that leaves the webhook endpoint completely unauthenticated in the default config. Prefer a hard fail (500 or 501) when the secret is missing so it forces the operator to configure it, rather than silently accepting unsigned events.

extras.py _ensure_stripe_catalog(): calls stripe.Product.list(active=True, limit=100).auto_paging_iter() and scans metadata for each product — O(N) per checkout on catalog-cold-start. Also calls stripe.Price.list(lookup_keys=...) per plan. Cache the resolved price IDs after first resolution.

extras.py _init_storage caches _storage_key['value'] in a module-level dict — this is thread-safe under uvicorn's single-process default but will each worker have its own cache. Not a bug, but worth noting for horizontal scaling.

extras.py CheckoutRequest.origin_url is passed through unvalidated into success_url/cancel_url. A malicious authenticated caller could set origin_url=https://evil.com/... — the Stripe checkout would then redirect there on success. Consider whitelisting origin_url against PUBLIC_APP_URL or the request Origin header.

extras.py ALLOWED_UPLOAD_MIMES trusts the client-provided Content-Type header. Consider magic-byte sniffing (python-magic or similar) to verify actual file type matches the claimed MIME, especially for SVG (which can contain arbitrary JS if served with the wrong CSP).

server.py verify_api_key prefix indexing is now O(1) via db.api_keys.find({key_prefix: prefix, revoked: {$ne: True}}) — GOOD improvement over iter-7 which did full-table bcrypt scan. Backfill logic for legacy keys without key_prefix is correct.

extras.py coupon_download_png renders a fixed-layout 1200x630 PNG with DejaVuSans fonts — no fallback if fonts unavailable (falls back to ImageFont.load_default() which is a tiny bitmap). Acceptable but the 'load_default' path produces unreadable output; consider bundling a TTF font in the app.

extras.py upload path derives filename ext from file.filename.split('.')[-1] — no normalization/validation. A filename like 'evil.php.png' would land at path .../uploads/{ws}/{fid}.png (technically OK because content_type is separately validated), but consider explicit ext whitelisting.

extras.py CURRENCIES + FONTS are module-level Python lists served fresh on every request. Consider a functools.lru_cache-wrapped serializer or a static JSON asset with Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 (these never change at runtime).
